subject: Human Body
title: The Lymphatic System
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Lymphatic System.

hook.text: Swollen glands during a cold? That's your lymph nodes filling with immune cells preparing for battle.

buildup.text: The lymphatic system is a network of vessels and nodes that drains fluid from tissues and filters it for threats.

discovery.text: Lymph nodes are like security checkpoints. Fluid passes through and immune cells scan it for pathogens.

twist.text: You have about 600 lymph nodes. They cluster near joints, the neck, and the gut — invasion-prone areas of the body.

climax.text: The lymphatic system is immune surveillance. It gives immune cells a place to meet, coordinate, and launch responses.

punchline.text: Swollen glands mean your immune system is working, not failing.

quiz.question: What happens in lymph nodes during an infection?
options: Red blood cells are produced to replace losses
Immune cells scan fluid for pathogens and mount responses
Lymph fluid is converted into antibodies
